subject: ODC compute sponsorship inquiry — open-data workshop
messages:
From: Dr. Helena Ruiz <h.ruiz@univ-state.edu>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: ODC compute sponsorship inquiry — open-data workshop

Hi Olga,

I hope you’re well — I’m writing on behalf of the Open Data Consortium (ODC). We run an annual week-long open-data workshop for graduate students and civic researchers; this year it’s scheduled for Jan 18–22, 2027. We are hoping Redwood would consider a compute sponsorship (credits or a short trial extension) to support hands-on sessions where attendees will run models on public datasets and prototype small apps.

Quick context: ODC is a non-profit consortium of 12 universities and civic partners. Last year’s workshop had ~65 attendees; this year we’re planning 80–100. The workshop includes four half-day guided labs that will generate short generation workloads (chat/assistant prompts + embeddings for retrieval). Estimated peak concurrency is ~15 simultaneous users, with rough per-day token estimates in the 400–800k token range across the cohort.

What we are requesting: 90 days of promotional credits (or an equivalent hosted-trial extension) to cover workshop usage and immediate post-workshop follow-on projects for a subset of participants (about 10 teams). If possible, we’d like a conditional waiver for any overage on the day of the workshop (we can set usage caps).

Attached: workshop agenda and the ODC charter. Happy to fill out the standard sponsorship form or answer questions. We often work with vendors on MOU language and can accept reasonable terms (we prefer a simple sponsorship MOU).

Next steps: could you point me to who owns promotions/partner credits, and an approximate timeline for decision? If it helps, I can share the short project list and a baseline SOW for the lab sessions.

Thanks —
Helena

Hi Helena — great to hear from you and thanks for the materials. I’ve looped in Rishi (sales lead for academic & non-profit programs) and Grace from CS who helps with onboarding workshops.

A few quick asks that will speed up review:
- A very short attendee breakdown (students vs researchers vs external partners) and expected peak concurrency per lab session.
- Per-day estimated token/embedding counts if you have them (your 400–800k/day estimate is helpful; if you can provide ranges per lab that’s ideal).
- Confirmation the data used in labs is public / non-sensitive (we do have stricter review for customer PII or private datasets).

Operational note: we typically handle sponsorships one of two ways — a hosted promotional credit applied to the ODC billing account, or a short dedicated trial for higher concurrency labs. Rishi and Grace can propose the right vehicle; we’ll need a short SOW (1–2 paragraphs) and a signed MOU.

I’ll ask Rishi to provision an approval path and a baseline offer. If you have preferred timing for a quick 20‑minute sync this week, let us know.

Best,
Olga
Senior Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference

Hi Helena — thanks for the clear note and materials, and thanks Olga for the intro. Quick summary from Redwood side and a proposed offer: 

Proposal (approval-in-principle):
- Promotional hosted credit: $12,000 in Redwood promotional credits valid for 90 days from issuance.
- Alternative (if you prefer higher concurrency during the on-site labs): a 30-day Dedicated trial (up to 4x A100-equivalent) with a cap on sustained concurrent users; the Dedicated option requires a short MOU and a technical checklist for network/keys.

Conditions and asks:
- Use limited to public datasets / workshop exercises (no sensitive PII).
- We’ll provision scoped API keys and set daily usage caps; overages will not be billed automatically — we’ll contact the ODC lead for approval before any charge.
- Signed MOU and brief SOW (1–2 paragraphs) describing the workshop labs and participant numbers.
- We will ask the consortium to include Redwood in workshop materials as a sponsor (logo + brief blurb).

Next steps:
1) If the promo credit works, I’ll open a HubSpot sponsorship record and generate a DocuSign MOU.
2) If you prefer the Dedicated trial, we’ll schedule an ops call to confirm network and capacity needs (we typically need 48–72 hours to provision).

If you can send the attendee breakdown and the one-paragraph SOW, I’ll file this for final sign-off today and aim to get the DocuSign out tomorrow.

Best regards,
Rishi
Senior Manager, Academic & Non-Profit Sales
Redwood Inference
